subject: Making awkward kitchen spaces useful
hook: Every kitchen has a spot nobody knows what to do with. Here are five, and what to put there.
ig:
Every kitchen has a spot nobody knows what to do with. Here are five, and what to put there.

Off-the-shelf kitchens come in set widths, so awkward bits of a room usually end up filled with a panel. With bespoke units, those gaps can earn their keep.

1. Blind corners: pull-out fittings or drawers either side, so nothing gets lost at the back.
2. Narrow gaps: a pull-out made to the exact width for trays, oils or boards.
3. Boxed-in pipes: units in front with a removable panel, so access is never lost.
4. The boiler: a tall housing that hides it while keeping ventilation and service access.
5. Chimney breast recesses: shelving or tall storage built to the exact depth.

The trick is spotting them at the survey stage. We measure every bow, pipe and recess so the design uses the room you've actually got.

fb:
Plenty of kitchens in older Staffordshire houses have the same quirks: a chimney breast, a boiler on the wrong wall, pipes boxed in at odd heights, and a corner that swallows saucepans.

The good news is that a bespoke kitchen doesn't have to work around those spots by covering them with panels. Built to the exact measurements, they can become pull-outs, tall storage or shelving that fits properly.

We've put five of the most common awkward spots in the carousel, with what we'd typically do with each. Which one is in your kitchen?
